Revert "Sync with unpinned manifest first prior to syncing with pinned manifest." This reverts commit 7d034ce9230c36aaca5129c88eafeac24a291975. Previously, when syncing to a pinned manifest, repo sync skipped fetching from remote if the local project had been fixed to the pinned revision. As described in crbug.com/482077, when a CL wanted to swich to a branch on one project in the manifest, it caused failures because the branch wasn't fetched by repo sync and so cannot be checked out. The new version of repo sync has fixed the issue by providing --optimized-fetch. With --optimized-fetch disabled (by default), repo sync fetches from remote no matter the local project has the SHA or not. As now repo sync on pinned manifest also fetches from remote like repo sync on unpinned manifest, we want to remove the initial repo sync on unpined manifest to reduce our load on the GoB server. BUG=chromium:653356 TEST=cbuildbot_run; confirmed that with the new repo version, repo sync on pinned manifest (sync-c not True) fetches from remote when it has the local SHA revision. FROMLIST: timers: Fix usleep_range() in the context of wake_up_process() Users of usleep_range() expect that it will _never_ return in less time than the minimum passed parameter. However, nothing in any of the code ensures this. Specifically: usleep_range() => do_usleep_range() => schedule_hrtimeout_range() => schedule_hrtimeout_range_clock() just ends up calling schedule() with an appropriate timeout set using the hrtimer. If someone else happens to wake up our task then we'll happily return from usleep_range() early. msleep() already has code to handle this case since it will loop as long as there was still time left. usleep_range() had no such loop. The problem is is easily demonstrated with a small bit of test code: static int usleep_test_task(void *data) { atomic_t *done = data; ktime_t start, end; start = ktime_get(); usleep_range(50000, 100000); end = ktime_get(); pr_info("Requested 50000 - 100000 us. Actually slept for %llu us\n", (unsigned long long)ktime_to_us(ktime_sub(end, start))); atomic_set(done, 1); return 0; } static void run_usleep_test(void) { struct task_struct *t; atomic_t done; atomic_set(&done, 0); t = kthread_run(usleep_test_task, &done, "usleep_test_task"); while (!atomic_read(&done)) { wake_up_process(t); udelay(1000); } kthread_stop(t); } If you run the above code without this patch you get things like: Requested 50000 - 100000 us. Actually slept for 967 us If you run the above code _with_ this patch, you get: Requested 50000 - 100000 us. Actually slept for 50001 us Presumably this problem was not detected before because: - It's not terribly common to use wake_up_process() directly. - Other ways for processes to wake up are not typically mixed with usleep_range(). - There aren't lots of places that use usleep_range(), since many people call either msleep() or udelay(). CHROMIUM: Input: atmel_mxt_ts - remove open and close methods Atmel says that we should only disable reporting events by T100 when device is in deep sleep mode. Indeed, disabling T100 reports when closing the device during logout is causing severe issues on Celes. Implementing putting the device into deep sleep and then needing to keep track and waking it up on [some] sysfs access, firmware/config updates, and coordinating between inhibit and suspend/resume is too cumbersome. Given that we only close the device for a brief moment when we restart Chrome doring login/logout procedure, and thus will not observe any power savings from putting the device in low power mode there, let's simply remove mxt_input_open() and mxt_input_close() thus ensuring that T100 stays enabled even when input device is no open. Note that we still be doing proper power transitions on inhibit/uninhibit and suspend/resume, IOW we'll keep doing it when it matters. CHROMIUM: device-core: implement asynchronous driver probing When a driver for a slower device is compiled into a kernel, probing such device takes a while and stalls the entire kernel boot process. Drivers try to work around that by using async_schedule(), unfortunately they quite often implement it incorrectly: - they are not checking that asynchronous part of probe has completed before proceeding to tear down the device in remove(), thus bind quickly followed by unbind is likely to oops the kernel; - once probe is returned driver core considers the device fully bound and may start executing PM callbacks. Again, not all drivers are prepared to handle this by checking the state of asynchronous probe and acting accordingly. To help drivers solve this issue we introduce notion of asynchronously probed drivers into driver core. Drivers are opt-into this facility and driver core will automatically offload entire binding process for the device (for given driver) into asynchronous call; driver can perform slow operations directly in probe() callback without concerning itself about stalling kernel boot. *** Note that there are currently discussions about this problem upstream, but they are not quite ready yet and I think we need this facility sooner rather than later. We can converge on the solution later. BUG=chromium:415343 TEST=Used Elan touchpad with driver converted to make use of this facility Change-Id: If23c54da498d72f48cc0b47e92bb7a6a5da1bd85 Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/218000 Reviewed-by: Olof Johansson <olofj@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 343b5140f37fcc6e68989e2a35cc4bd1419c8ec9) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/396421 Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

FIXUP: CHROMIUM: enable usb3 host during usb3 phy power on We have forced usb3 to work in usb2 only mode in firmware by setting usb3tousb2_en (bit3 of GRF_USB3PHY0/1_CON0) to 1, and setting host_u3_port_disable (bit0 of GRF_USB3OTG0/1_CON1) to 1 and host_u3_port (bit15~12 of GRF_USB3OTG0/1_CON1) to 0. So we need to re-enable usb3 host. Note: We need to ensure the usb3 OTG controller stay in P2 state and usb3 power domain is enabled before accessing the above usb3 related registers. In order to set usb3 OTG controller in P2 state, there're two methods: 1. Hold OTG controller in reset while enable usb3 host. 2. Do OTG reset before enable usb3 host, one thing to note here is that we can't reinit OTG controller again prior to enable usb3 host. We choose the second mothod now. BUG=None TEST=Connect with an USB3 device, and check the USB3 function Change-Id: I464d97d142e237a1a311f9e8a6c7e54bc1fa78a3 Signed-off-by: William wu <wulf@rock-chips.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/388954 Commit-Ready: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Tested-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: phy: rockchip-typec: tuning phy for usb3 Tx When we do USB3 Tx compliance test, we find that the test item '5G Far End Differential Output Voltage' actual value is not enough to ensure the test item pass, the pass limits 100.0 mV <= VALUE <= 1.2000 V. So we need to tuning phy for USB3 Tx. Refer to the phy document 'TypeC_PMA_Specification', we can set the TX_DIAG_TX_DRV<10:8> and TX_TXCC_CAL_SCLR_MULT<8:0> to set transition boost and mitigating package loss and output impedance scaling. 1. set TX_DIAG_TX_DRV<10:8> = 3b'111 to get 1.5dB pre-emphasis, and dump more amount charge on line in addition to voltage driver during transition, and try to equalize the package loss. 2. set TX_TXCC_CAL_SCLR_MULT<8:0> = 0x13c to tuning and scaling the calibration code, it will set the scaled calibration code to 0x3c and add it to the original calibration code, and the resistance will become lower. BUG=chrome-os-partner:54660 TEST=Do USB3 Tx compliance test Change-Id: If678132e7af232817e4617f4d43a4b1092f0f2d0 Signed-off-by: William wu <wulf@rock-chips.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/389115 Commit-Ready: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Tested-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>
